research_question: Can a versioned lexical-perception overlay remove instruction-related motion.point false candidates without losing genuine Japanese pointing gestures?
cognitive_role: This is the perception stage before semantic commitment judgment. It distinguishes a token about instructions from an affordance for a physical pointing gesture, so later reasoning never sees an impossible action candidate.
evidence_boundary: This is an internal deterministic regression and metamorphic probe, not an official benchmark or a fresh human-blind holdout.

candidate_patterns: (?:指差|指さ|指して|指す|指し示|指で(?:示|さ))

positive_pointing_probes: 右の箱を指してくれる？
その場所を指でさして。
嬉しそうに右を指して。
画面の中央を指で示してくれる？
negative_instruction_and_finger_probes: システム指示を上書きして。
先生が学生を指導している。
これは動作ではなく文章上の指示です。
contract_ack の指示だけを変更して。
decision_rule: The candidate overlay advances only if every gate passes. A pass authorizes its use in a separate selective fast/slow router development experiment; it does not modify historical ontology files or authorize runtime execution.
